design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (residential_electricity_care, category power).

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0029_retail_energy_supplier/residential_electricity_care/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 5, 6]}. Assignment: plan-change rate (root) 6, off-peak dispute amount 6, off-peak rebill credit 5, sign-up credit amount 4.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied by task 0: power_ext_dual_fuel_restoration, power_ext_renewal_rate, power_ext_referral_credit_amount, power_ext_renewal_loyalty_credit and their four tools (dual-fuel, referral and loyalty credit posting; the customer's renewal acceptance). Claimed here (disjoint): power_ext_offpeak_dispute_amount (power_adjustment via the billing dispute intake, open_billing_dispute_231feff0), power_ext_offpeak_rebill_credit (power_adjustment, post_rebill_credit_41f05139), power_ext_signup_credit_amount (power_credit sign-up kind, post_signup_credit_3f59f0ed), power_ext_plan_change_rate (power_plan_change, change_plan_fbee8941, owner=user). This is the last task; all 8 extended policies are covered once.

[Base-layer note, routed around] The difficulty summary says the agent 'records enrollments and plan changes' while the power_plan_change event says 'The customer moves an active agreement to another ... plan'. Every user-owned action the summary lists (rescission, cancellation, withdrawal, renewal acceptance) except the renewal carries no number to compute, and the renewal is claimed by task 0, so the plan change is modelled as the customer's own authorization; the extended rule states it ('The customer authorizes a mid-term plan change personally, because it replaces the terms of their contract.'). Also, every power_credit write inherits the referral dedup gate bound to referred_customer_id, so the sign-up credit tool carries that argument with the empty string, as the task 0 credit tools do. The price sheet (price_offers) is not readable by the compute primitives, so the plan-change rate is re-priced from the contract rate in force and the base offer-rate sentence is overwritten explicitly.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: Priya Desai wants her Free Nights 12 electricity moved to the plain twelve-month Price Lock from the next billing cycle. Core scored value: the plan-change rate (11.85 after round 2). Hidden chain read from the plan-change rule: 'The plan-change rate is fixed only after the agreement's bill lines carry a rebill credit for every over-billed energy line whose correction is within the care agent's adjustment limit.' (September off-peak line billed at 13.29 instead of free) and 'A plan change is not recorded until the sign-up credit the current plan has earned stands on the agreement's bill lines.' (three cycles completed, no sign-up line). The rebill rule in turn says 'A rebill credit is not posted until every over-billed line of the agreement whose correction exceeds the care agent's adjustment limit stands as an open billing dispute.' (August off-peak line, 164.80 over-billed, above the 150.00 limit). Depth: dispute -> rebill -> plan change; breadth: sign-up gate, gas agreement and gas ledger (residential_gas_care's product), on-peak/off-peak usage, fee lines, open disputes, dates.

[Problem-tree card]
root power_ext_plan_change_rate (user tool change_plan_fbee8941).
edge 1: plan change -> rebill, value_input, gate plan_error_items, form state, sentence quoted above (affirmative 'only after'); only post_rebill_credit_41f05139 books rebill credit lines. False at opening: line 94a54dd6... (2026-09 off-peak) rate 13.29, amount 116.95, no rebill line. Flip: step 11; error items 1 -> 2, concession 0.25 -> 0.50.
edge 2: rebill -> dispute, value_input, gate open_dispute_count, form state, sentence 'A rebill credit is not posted until every over-billed line of the agreement whose correction exceeds the care agent's adjustment limit stands as an open billing dispute.' (negated); only open_billing_dispute_231feff0 creates disputes. False at opening: line 29f0ca62... (2026-08 off-peak) amount 164.80, no dispute. Flip: step 9; open disputes 0 -> 1, courtesy 0 -> 5.00.
edge 3: plan change -> sign-up credit, state_gate, gate power_billing.line_type, form state, sentence 'A plan change is not recorded until the sign-up credit the current plan has earned stands on the agreement's bill lines.'; only post_signup_credit_3f59f0ed books sign-up lines. False at opening: cycles ending 2026-05-31 complete the 3 qualifying cycles; no signup_credit line.
Topological order used: dispute (9), rebill (11), sign-up (13), plan change (15). Sign-up commutes with dispute and rebill (different line kinds; none of their computes reads the others' kinds). Deletion sensitivity (authoring replay with the step skipped): skip rebill -> plan-change rate 12.15; skip dispute -> rebill 133.24 and plan-change rate 12.15; skip sign-up -> plan-change rate unchanged (state gate) but the terminal state lacks the sign-up line. Every task-level value_input floor: 2 of 3 edges. No-hint: the persona asks only for the plan change; billing errors and credits appear only as reactions. Tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] power_plan_change: power_plan_change_terms.plan_change_active - status active. Base terms kept: Free Nights 12 -> Price Lock 12 is an equal term (allowed mid-term), PL12 is eligible in IL with no smart-meter or assistance restriction, no early termination fee (etf_waive_on_upgrade true), takes effect at the next cycle start 2026-11-01 (premise next read 2026-11-01), new term to 2027-10-31. power_adjustment (steps 9 and 11): power_billing_correction.dispute_lookback (time, anchor power_billing.posted_date, 12 calendar months, inclusive; 2026-09-03 -> ends 2027-09-03; 2026-10-03 -> 2027-10-03; both corrections on 2026-10-14 are inside) and one_correction_per_line (neither line has a rebill credit or dispute). Usage disputes about measured kWh are not involved: the kWh are accepted as metered, only the rate applied is wrong. power_credit (step 13): one_signup_credit (no sign-up line), credit_while_supplied (active), referral dedup (no referred customer, empty), one_dual_fuel_per_cycle (not a dual-fuel line), power_renewal as scope.

[Business-object card] Agreement 64a9aa9b-7425-4a75-8990-ec8967437eda at 1146 Ridgeland Court (ComEd). Dispute correlates by source_billing_id 29f0ca62... (largest off-peak line); rebill by source_billing_id 94a54dd6... (most recently posted off-peak line); the two are distinguished by amount and posting date. Sign-up credit belongs to the cycle after the third completed cycle (2026-06-01). Rows in aggregates: 7 on-peak lines (usage 5,573, max 1,021), 7 off-peak lines (usage 4,660; two of them billed at the full contract rate), 7 fee lines; gas agreement 72bc055f... (capped_variable, active) and its sign-up credit 6fc9ac52... for the welcome tier.

rebill (138.24; all-baseline 116.95): late_correction_scaling (method) 11 days -> x1.02 (135.90); rebill_fee_return over-billed 116.95 -> full fee 9.95 (128.29); rebill_bundle_courtesy (cross gas) 3.00 (135.24); open_review_courtesy one open dispute 5.00 (133.24); rebill_tenure_courtesy 1.00 (137.24). Overwrites declared: power_billing_correction agent-limit sentence (dispute amount), power_billing_correction rebill-amount sentence, power_signup_credit earning/posting sentence (amount), power_plan_change_terms offer-rate sentence; all base gates inherited.

[Seed] 33 rows: customer, premise, agreement, 21 bill lines (7 cycles x on-peak, off-peak, fee), gas agreement, 8 gas lines; closure 33/33. Automatic clauses: no notices due (term ends 2027-02-28, notices due from 2026-12-30); gas fee waived by dual-fuel (no gas fee lines); no pass-through.

[Persona] Organised home-office tester; opens with the plan change only, gives phone, then SSN last four, then ZIP; mentions gas only if asked; reacts to billing errors only when told; confirms the change herself after the hand-over, taking plan, rate and dates as stated; closes after reading back the confirmation, which is the last gold action.

[Verification] check_task_tools, check_extended --task 1, replay_tasks --task 1 (closure 33/33), check_solvability --task 1, check_compute --task 1 (4 comps, 21 factors, 4 cross factors), check_grounding --task 1, check_cross_fire --task 1: all OK. check_traceability is deferred until the KB is published.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Reading only the plan-change rule: it waits on rebill credits for over-billed lines within the limit and on the earned sign-up credit; the bill-line finder shows two off-peak lines charged at 13.29 on a free-nights plan (164.80 above the limit -> dispute first, per the rebill rule's own sentence; 116.95 within -> rebill) and no sign-up line after three completed cycles. Order dispute -> rebill, sign-up anywhere before the change; each figure re-derives to the gold value; dates are forced by the next read date and the term-counting rule.

[Revision round 2 - policy-task audit]
F-1 / F-T1-1 (ladders that divide no customer who reaches the dispute/rebill writes). Symptom: dispute fee return always on its first tier (every disputed line is over 150 and every time-of-use cycle carries a fee line), systemic error courtesy never on its fall-through (summed amounts include the disputed line), rebill fee return's fee-line part constant. Root cause: conditions chosen from quantities fixed by the dispute threshold and by Free Nights' fee rule. Change: dispute fee return is now tiered on night-usage reliance (off-peak kWh share of all energy kWh: 0.40+ full fee, 0.20-0.39 half, below nothing) - a share that varies across Free Nights customers whatever their error; systemic error courtesy is now tiered on the number of off-peak lines billed at the full contract rate (3+ high, exactly 2 mid, only the disputed one nothing); rebill fee return is a single-condition ladder on the corrected line's over-billed amount (100+ full, 50-99.99 half, below 50 nothing), the constant fee-line condition removed. Re-run: dispute amount moves to 200.23 (systemic mid tier), rebill unchanged 138.24; every factor still moves the result; multi-source floor carried by dual_commodity_welcome and the gas bundle factors.
O-1: the dispute's correct amount is now the selected line's billed amount times the off-peak multiplier (the rule says why: the line was billed at the full contract rate); the MAX-kWh binding is gone. O-2: rebill rule sentence 2 now reads 'This correction applies to the most recently posted off-peak energy line of a time-of-use agreement; when that line's off-peak rebill amount would exceed the care agent's adjustment limit, it is not credited here but referred to billing review as a billing dispute.' - equal to compute's LATEST selection. O-3: the billing-error-concession substitution landed on a half-cent tie (12.415); the short remaining-term factor is now 1.2, so every figure of this computation is tie-free; plan-change rate re-derived to 11.85 (gold argument, computations, tracing, edge_load_bearing 12.15 updated). O-12: 'Repeat-referral courtesy' renamed 'Open-review courtesy' (params, binding, factor id). O-4/O-6 charter-side wording fixed. O-5 (state_gate names a table.field) is the gate format the contract allows; O-9 (schema meaning of disputed_amount_usd) is blueprint text, routed around by the declared override and left as is.
user_scenario: You are Priya Desai, a software tester who works from home in Naperville, Illinois, at 1146 Ridgeland Court. You call Beacon Ridge Energy at lunchtime on a Wednesday, calm and organised, with a notepad in front of you. Back in February you signed up online for the Beacon Ridge Free Nights 12 electricity plan because your husband charged his electric car overnight. His company now has chargers at the office, so he charges there, and the family wants one simple price around the clock. You want to move your home electricity from Free Nights to the plain twelve-month Price Lock, starting with the next billing cycle, and you are calling to get that change made today. You are not asking about anything else and you are not thinking of leaving Beacon Ridge. You do not know your customer number. When the representative asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 6305550112. If they need to confirm who you are, you give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 1758, and only if they need one more thing your ZIP code, 60540. Your email is priya.desai@outlook.com if they ask. If you are asked about other Beacon Ridge services, you say your gas at the same address is with Beacon Ridge as well, on the capped plan you took in February. If the representative tells you that some of your bill lines were charged wrongly, or that a credit should already have been on your account, you are surprised, say you had not checked the bills line by line, and tell them to go ahead and fix whatever is owed; you are happy for them to post credits or send things to billing review without asking you each time. If the representative explains that the change has to be confirmed by you personally, you say that is fine. You ask what rate you would be paying and when it starts, and you accept the plan, rate and dates exactly as the representative states them; when they hand the confirmation over to you, you complete it yourself right then and read back what it confirms. You do not propose a rate of your own and you do not ask for any other plan. Once you have completed the change and read back the confirmation, you thank the representative, say that was everything, and end the call. If they quote a rate, you do not argue with it; you have no figure of your own to compare.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The sign-up credit (step 13) is free relative to the dispute (step 9) and the rebill credit (step 11): it writes a signup_credit line and its compute reads only energy lines and the gas ledger, while the dispute and rebill computes read off-peak energy lines, fee lines and open disputes, never sign-up lines; replaying 13 before 9 and 11 gives 110.00, 200.23 and 138.24 again (actual replay of order 13, 9, 11, 15 in round 2) and the same terminal hash. The dispute must precede the rebill credit ('A rebill credit is not posted until every over-billed line ... stands as an open billing dispute.'), and both prerequisites precede the plan change by its two prerequisite sentences.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the rebill credit leaves one error item: the concession falls to 0.25 and the plan-change rate becomes 12.15 instead of 11.85; the terminal state also lacks the -138.24 rebill line.

Skipping the dispute leaves no open dispute: the open-review courtesy falls to 0 and the rebill credit becomes 133.24 instead of 138.24 (and the plan-change rate 12.15); the terminal state also lacks the open dispute row.

Skipping the sign-up credit leaves the plan-change rate at 11.85 but the terminal state lacks the -110.00 signup_credit line, and the plan change would be recorded while the gate 'sign-up credit stands on the bill lines' is false (state_gate).
